newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Charge expected over Irish journalist's murder.
newsitem.headline: Charge expected over Irish journalist's murder.

text.p: Police said on Friday they expected to charge a man with conspiracy to murder Ireland's foremost investigative reporter, Veronica Guerin, who was killed in June.
They said the man was among dozens of people who had been questioned since Guerin was shot by a man on a motorbike at traffic lights outside Dublin. They gave no further details.

Police, who believe the shooting was ordered by a drugs baron who feared Guerin's investigations, had not previously laid any charges. They say their investigations have centred around the murky drugs underworld existing in Ireland.
The murder provoked outrage in Ireland and led the government to draw up tough anti-crime measures and hold a special summer recess sitting of parliament.
Guerin, who worked for Ireland's Sunday Independent newspaper, was married with one child and had been shot at twice before.

Drugs traffickers use Ireland as a trans-shipment point for drugs destined for other parts of Europe. The republic also has its own drugs problem, with an estimated 10,000 heroin addicts in Dublin alone.
